title: Undertrials During the year 2000, the highest number of undertrial prisoners (44121) in various jails was reported from Uttar Pradesh. This was followed by Bihar (29891), Madhya Pradesh (15578) and Maharashtra (15002). The other states which also reported high number of undertrials in their custody during 2000 were Orissa (10087), Andhra Pradesh (8993), Punjab (8389), Rajasthan (8362), West Bengal (7964), Haryana (7815), Karnataka (7384), Gujarat (5193) and UT of Dethi (8650). Some of the States had large number of the undertrials kept in the Central Jails. The number of undertrials kept in the Central Jails of the various States were Maharashtra (8907), Bihar (6380), Punjab (6295), Madhya Pradesh (4196), Karnataka (4080), Andhra Pradesh (3095), West Bengal (2879), Rajasthan (2385), Uttar Pradesh (1414), Gujarat (1286), Kerala (1215) and UT of Delhi (8282). The other states had either kept most of the undertrials in district jails or sub jails. Uttar Pradesh (42203), Bihar (16457), Maharashtra (5966), Haryana (4803), Madhya Pradesh (4522), Assam (3940), Orissa (3885), Rajasthan (3620), Andhra Pradesh (2304), West Bengal (2282) and Gujarat (2143) mainly accommodated the undertrials in the District jails. Bihar (7027), Madhya Pradesh (6860), Orissa (4872) and Andhra Pradesh (3492) had lodged considerable number of undertrials in the sub jails also. The jails exclusively meant to lodge women prisoners reported population of undertrials from Delhi (368), Punjab (124), Andhra Pradesh (102), Tamil Nadu (34), Rajasthan (28), Bihar (27), Kerala (17), West Bengal (10), Orissa & Tripura (8 each) and
